summary_en: E-Guardian announced Q&A disclosure regarding the acquisition of Outsourcing Communications (OSCOM) as a wholly owned subsidiary, pursuant to a share transfer agreement executed on 2026-05-22. Deal value, purchase price per share, and acquisition timing not disclosed in this Q&A document. The acquisition marks E-Guardian's entry into new BPO domains (back-office, sales/marketing, IT systems) and reflects strategy to deploy the AI-BPO model across M&A targets to convert labour-intensive operations into high-margin recurring revenue.
title_en: Notice of Public Disclosure of Q&A Regarding E-Guardian Inc. Second Quarter FY2026 Results and Full Subsidiary Acquisition of Outsourcing Communications Inc.
translation_en_brief:
On 2026-06-02, E-Guardian filed a Q&A disclosure addressing investor questions regarding its acquisition of Outsourcing Communications (OSCOM) as a wholly owned subsidiary. The company executed a share transfer agreement on 2026-05-22. This disclosure provides management commentary on the rationale and integration strategy, but does not restate deal value, share count, purchase price per share, or expected closing date—those details were disclosed separately on 2026-05-22.

Management characterised the OSCOM acquisition as E-Guardian's entry point into adjacent BPO domains including back-office operations, sales and marketing, and IT systems BPO, beyond its existing monitoring and audit service lines. The company intends to embed its proprietary AI-BPO model into OSCOM's operations to shift from labour-intensive, cost-reduction-focused outsourcing toward high-margin, recurring-revenue BPO in which artificial intelligence performs routine tasks and learns continuously from customer data, enabling profitability to rise as volume scales.

Management noted plans for multiple M&A completions over the current and next fiscal year in the 100-million to several-billion-yen range, subject to confirmation of AI-BPO synergies and preservation of financial health. The OSCOM acquisition exemplifies the broader shift away from labour-dependent growth toward AI-augmented service delivery across the group.
